children: New Delhi, Oct. 22 -- Dividend, bonus, stock split record date: Shares of Tech Mahindra, Indian Railway Finance Corporation, LTM, ICICI Lombard General Insurance, Modison Limited, Oberoi Realty, etc will remain in focus during Thursday's trading session due to their upcoming record dates for dividend, stock split, bonus shares.

More than 10 companies have fixed Friday, October 23, as the record date to determine eligibility of shareholders. As the Indian stock market follows the T+1 settlement cycle, investors must own the stock before the record date to qualify for the corporate actions.
Hence, Thursday, October 22, effectively becomes the last day to buy these stocks and become eligible for stock split, bonus or dividend.

360 One WAM Limited, Artemis Electricals and Projects Ltd, Bhansali Engineering Polymers, Garuda Construction and Engineering, HDB Financial Services, IRF, LTM, Modison, Tech Mahindra, etc have fixed Friday, as the record date for interim dividend. Which effectively makes Thursday as the last day for investors to qualify for the payout.
Titan Biotech has fixed Friday as record date for bonus issue in the ratio of 1:4. Whereas, Azad India Mobility Ltd will determine eligibility of shareholders for stock split from Rs.10 to Rs.2.

The Indian stock market formed a bearish candle in the previous session with a "lower high and lower low" signalling continuation of the corrective bias. The Nifty 50 Index closed below the 20 days EMA in the previous session.

"Nifty despite starting on a positive note failed to move above Monday's high 23,175 and dragged sharply lower signaling continuation of the corrective consolidation in the range of 22,500-23,150. Nifty has support at 22,500-22,400 levels being the 80% retracement of the last two weeks pullback 22180-23,175," explained Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research, Bajaj Broking.

"On the higher side key level to watch is Monday's high of 23,175, only a move above the same will signal pullback towards 23,300 and 23,500 levels in the coming sessions being the 50% retracement of the entire recent decline from 24,774 to 22,180," Mukherjee added.
